text:
Rina: Quick sync thread re: reserved pools SLA wording + burst smoothing behavior. ACME wants explicit no-hard-eviction guarantee during their local business hours. Need product + eng alignment before we commit.
Arjun: Agree we should avoid hard evictions for reserved pools. Two levers: smoothing token bucket + prioritized spillover to cheaper variants.
Paul: Counterpoint: unlimited soft-spill can soak capacity and hurt other reserved customers. We need quantitative guardrails.
Nina: Legal flagged we must list exact failure modes and remediation steps. Not OK with vague language like "best effort."
Rina: Proposal: 1) No hard evictions during business hours for committed reserved pools. 2) If capacity exhausted, apply soft-spill for up to 60s window, then controlled throttling. 3) Autoscale can trigger but with cooldown to avoid oscillation.
Arjun: Config sketch: `reserved_policy: { business_hours_protection: true, soft_spill_window_s: 60, throttle_step_qps: 5, autoscale_cooldown_s: 90 }`
metrics-bot: Quick metric pull: reserved_pool.acme-prod.p99 7d = 380ms (burst windows), p95 = 95ms.
ACME-ops: From our side, latency is preferred over errors. We can accept up to 500ms p99 during brief spikes but not 5xx. We want telemetry tags to debug per-customer events.
Paul: If we allow 60s soft-spill, need a guard: if error rate >0.5% during the window then escalate to emergency throttle and page SRE. Also cap total soft-spill throughput as percent of pool capacity.
Nina: Legal asks for a short SLA clause: define business hours, define no-hard-eviction promise, enumerate allowed degradations (latency up to X, queued responses), and remedies (credits, prioritized fix). I'll draft.
Rina: Launch gating idea: canary with ACME traffic replay for 72h, pass criteria: no hard evictions, p99<=420ms (canary), error_rate<0.1%. For GA tighten to p99<=350ms and error_rate<0.05% for 7d.
Arjun: Implementation detail: token-bucket smoothing with adaptive refill based on short-term capacity signal. Start with fixed bucket (size=250, refill=6 qps) for canary, tune later.
Paul: Need to simulate multi-tenant interference. I'll run a 48h multi-tenant sim: ACME replay + 5 other reserved clients at 60-80% baseline. Will report p99 per-tenant and eviction counts.
ACME-ops: Please include our spike shape: sustained baseline + periodic 30s 3x bursts every 8 minutes.
metrics-bot: Scheduled sim dataset: /sims/1779991234/multi_tenant_acme_replay (ETA 36h).
Rina: Ops runbook changes: add a "reserved-burst-handling" play with steps: enable soft-spill, monitor tag `reserved_burst=true`, apply throttle thresholds, invoke emergency manual override.
Nina: I'll attach SLA draft to drive and link back once legal approves. Need product to sign off on numeric thresholds first.
Arjun: One more caution: autoscale cooldowns matter. If cooldown too short we oscillate; too long and customers see latency. Start with 90s for reserved pools and 120s for mixed pools.
Paul: After sims, if any hard-evictions occur, we'll implement preempt-credit accounting so that we can explain why an eviction happened and offer credits.
Rina: Action items: Paul run multi-tenant sims and post results (36h). Arjun implement canary config and feature flag `reserved_soft_spill_v1`. Nina draft SLA wording and loop legal. I'll ping ACME-ops with proposed canary windows.
ACME-ops: Thanks. We'll allocate a canary window next Tuesday and provide ops on-call.
Rina: Great. We'll reconvene in this thread with artifacts. Keep replies short here pls. :thumbsup:
